sentences.text:
The petitioners are before this Court seeking the following prayer:
"a) issue a writ of Certiorari or any other writ or order the Respondent to consider the application under Section 28A of Land Acquisition Act within reasonable time as prescribed this Hon'ble Court (Annexure - E-1, E-2, E-3 and E-4)
b) Grant such other relief or reliefs as this Hon'ble Court deems it fit to grant in the facts and circumstances of this case."

2. Heard Sri Ravindra P., learned counsel for petitioners, Sri Spoorthy Hegde N., learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 and Sri T.P.Vivekananda, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
3.

The backdrop of seeking reference of the applications of the petitioners filed under Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act') is that, the lands belonging to the petitioners become the subject matter of acquisition in January, 1992, by issuance of a preliminary NC:
2025:KHC:18588 HC-KAR notification.
The final notification was issued on 21.04.1998.
A general award comes to be passed on 15.07.1999.
The litigations thereafter galore between the parties.
On 11.08.2004, respondent No.2 is said to have deposited the compensation of Rs.1,93,937/- in favour of the petitioners.
The petitioners filed a miscellaneous first appeal seeking enhancement of compensation, which comes to be withdrawn seeking liberty to approach the appropriate forum.
It is then, applications under Section 18 of the Act to refer the matter to the reference Court.
After which, applications are filed under Section 28A of the Act seeking re-determination of compensation.
It is the applications seeking re-determination of the compensation is what has driven the petitioners to this Court in the subject petition.
4. Sri T.P.Vivekananda, learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that the applications of the petitioners, in strict consonance of law would be considered, if reasonable time is granted.
